Claim: The Trump administration "has banned the CDC even using the word 'transgender.'"
Ended: Aug 17, 2018 (PolitiFact False: CDC/HHS denied any word ban; guidance was budget-language advice)
Notes: Based on WaPo headline about avoiding words in budget docs; CDC Director and CDC spokeswoman said no ban.

Claim: You can see visits to Moscow made during the campaign by Paul Manafort and others (implying Manafort went).
Ended: May 19, 2017 (PolitiFact Mostly False: no public record Manafort went; overstated 'and others')
Notes: Carter Page went once; Flynn trip was before exclusive Trump-campaign role.

Claim: If Trump had done his job from the beginning on COVID-19, 'all the people would still be alive. All the people.'
Ended: Sept 18, 2020 (PolitiFact False: experts said many lives could have been saved, not every death)
Notes: Columbia and other studies estimated large averted deaths from earlier mitigation—not zero U.S. deaths.

Claim: Donald Trump asserted that immigrants would 'carve you up with a knife.'
Ended: Aug 9, 2019 (PolitiFact False; FactCheck.org same week: Trump referred to MS-13 gang members)
Notes: Oct 22, 2018 Houston rally line was about MS-13, not immigrants generally.

Claim: All of Trump's tax cuts 'went to folks at the top and corporations that pay no taxes' (audience got nothing).
Ended: April 30, 2019 (FactCheck.org: most households got a tax cut; TPC ~65%)
Notes: Higher earners gained more; claiming 'all' went only to the top is false.

Claim: 45 nations had already restricted travel from China before Trump moved; the U.S. 'started off awfully slow.'
Ended: April 6, 2020 (FactCheck.org: U.S. neither late nor first among peers after WHO PHEIC)
Notes: ThinkGlobalHealth tracker: dozens of countries moved in same WHO-window cluster as U.S.

Claim: After Las Vegas, Trump said he'd ban bump stocks—but 'Did he ban the bump stocks? No' because the NRA stopped him.
Ended: June 5, 2019 (FactCheck.org: ATF final rule banned bump stocks effective March 2019)
Notes: Speed/legislation critiques are separate; the ban did take effect.

Claim: Trump promised manufacturing jobs would stay but they're not / he failed to bring manufacturing jobs back (national impression).
Began: July 9–12, 2019 (Gillibrand CNN remarks + anti-Trump TV ad)
Ended: July 12, 2019 (FactCheck.org: net +~486k manufacturing jobs since Trump took office)
Who_Pushed_It: Sen. Kirsten Gillibrand; Gillibrand campaign ad citing MSNBC Lordstown framing
Approximate_Duration: days of tour/ad cycle until FactCheck
Deception_Form: cherry-picked plant closures as national trend
Notes: Local Rust Belt losses real; national BLS manufacturing employment rose.

Claim: Trump had to confess in writing in court to illegally diverting charitable contributions that were supposed to go to veterans.
Ended: Nov 21, 2019 (PolitiFact False: settlement admitted campaign control of fundraiser; funds reached veterans charities)
Notes: Judge found fiduciary breach aiding the campaign; not diversion away from veterans.

Claim: U.S. government wiretapped former Trump campaign chairman Paul Manafort under FISA (CNN exclusive).
Ended: Dec 9–17, 2019 (DOJ IG report contradicted; CNN editor's note acknowledging contradiction)
Approximate_Duration: ~2 years until IG report + editor's note
Notes: IG: Crossfire Hurricane team did not seek/seriously consider FISA on Manafort. CNN posted editor's note rather than full retraction.

Claim: Donald Trump stood on a debate stage and said wages in America are 'too high' (as if all wages).
Ended: July 26, 2016 (FactCheck.org: context was opposing a $15 minimum wage)
Who_Pushed_It: Sen. Bob Casey; Sen. Kirsten Gillibrand (DNC)
Notes: Trump clarified two days after Nov 2015 debate he meant minimum wage.

Claim: On average, middle-class families earning under ~$86,000 would see a tax increase under the Republican tax reform plan (Harris/Casey tweets).
Ended: Nov 2, 2017 (Washington Post Fact Checker: falsely claim; Four Pinocchios; tweets later deleted)
Who_Pushed_It: Sen. Kamala Harris; Sen. Bob Casey Jr.; other Senate Democrats
Notes: Subset facing increases misframed as typical/middle-class average outcome.

Claim: 129 million people with preexisting conditions could be denied coverage under Trump/GOP health repeal (Harris tweet).
Ended: May 10, 2017 (WaPo Fact Checker Three Pinocchios: HHS figure was broad potential exposure, not certain denials)
Notes: WaPo Three Pinocchios; user bar also includes Four Pinocchios—kept as named WaPo Fact Checker case.

Claim: Trump cut Justice Department funding to investigate domestic terrorist / white supremacist groups.
Ended: April 11, 2019 (PolitiFact Mostly False: cited DHS prevention grants, not DOJ/FBI investigative cuts)
Notes: CVE grant changes at DHS; no evidence FBI investigative funding cut as claimed.

Claim: Trump's whole health-care plan is a six-word plan: replace Obamacare with 'something so much better.'
Ended: July 27, 2016 (FactCheck.org: Trump had posted a multi-point health plan on his site)
Notes: Plan substance debatable; claim of no plan beyond six words was false.

Claim: Trump would cut taxes for the richest Americans at the expense of the middle class (implying middle class gets no relief).
Ended: July 26, 2016 (FactCheck.org: TPC—middle-income households get average ~$2,700 cut under Trump plan)
Notes: Distribution skewed upward, but middle class was not excluded from cuts.

Claim: The FBI gave Rudy Giuliani a 2019 defensive briefing warning he was a target of Russian disinformation (also claimed for OAN).
Began: April 29–30, 2021 (WaPo then NYT/NBC follow-ons after Giuliani raid)
Ended: May 1–3, 2021 (WaPo/NYT/NBC corrections; Poynter roundup)
Who_Pushed_It: The Washington Post; The New York Times; NBC News
Notes: NBC: briefing prepared but not delivered. Corrected stories removed assertions Giuliani/OAN received warnings.

Claim: National Guard troops withdrew from Los Angeles, Chicago, and Portland with no public acknowledgment from the White House/Pentagon.
Ended: Feb 11, 2026 (WaPo X correction noting Trump Truth Social announcement weeks earlier; prior post deleted)
Notes: Correction text: withdrew with no public acknowledgment other than Trump social post weeks earlier. Primary WaPo story: https://www.washingtonpost.com/national-security/2026/02/11/national-guard-los-angeles-chicago-portland/

Claim: Trump Media / Truth Social paid a $240,000 loan referral fee tied to a 'porn-friendly' bank trust stake narrative.
Ended: May 22, 2026 (WaPo Correction after discovery; court order notes Post admitted no such fee was paid)
Approximate_Duration: ~3 years until published Correction / litigation admission
Notes: Federal summary-judgment order quotes Correction: discovery established TMTG didn't pay the $240k referral fee. Suit later dismissed on actual-malice grounds.

Claim: Under Trump/DOGE, Social Security would communicate with the press and public exclusively via X (dropping press releases/Dear Colleague letters).
Began: April 2025 (WIRED report of internal meeting remarks; Warren and others amplified)
Ended: April 14, 2025 (SSA on X and to Newsweek: 'This is false'; continues any/all mediums; White House Rapid Response called Wired report fake)
Who_Pushed_It: WIRED (meeting report); Sen. Elizabeth Warren (amplifying); viral posts
Deception_Form: overstated internal plan as locked exclusive policy
Notes: WIRED quoted regional commissioner; SSA official channel denied exclusive-X shift. Include as named-outlet claim later contradicted by agency.

Claim: NYT reported Pax Silica consortium sought $4 trillion / $1 trillion committed investment and quoted Under Secretary Helberg calling Hormuz disruption 'a blessing.'
Ended: March 23 & March 29, 2026 (NYT corrections: >$1T AUM not $4T; not committed $1T; quote was 'a lesson' not 'a blessing')
Notes: Helberg posted full remarks; NYT Communications said errors corrected when aware. Secondary sources quote NYT correction boxes.

Claim: Trump left the Biden-Harris team the worst unemployment since the Great Depression.
Ended: Sept 11–17, 2024 (FactCheck.org False: Jan 2021 unemployment 6.4%, below many post-1930s peaks)
Notes: Also flagged again in FactCheck Harris jobs piece Sept 17, 2024.

Claim: ICE agents used / held a 5-year-old autistic girl in a way NBC initially framed as pressuring her father to surrender (later corrected as mischaracterization).
Ended: Sept 23, 2025 (NBC CORRECTION: earlier version mischaracterized ICE agents' activities in the video)
Notes: DHS said father fled vehicle and abandoned child; local police recovered child. Named-outlet correction on Trump-era ICE framing.

Claim: As president, Trump 'cut overtime benefits for millions of workers.'
Ended: Aug 19, 2024 (FactCheck.org: Trump raised OT threshold vs status quo; did not cut existing OT; fell short of Obama rule)
Who_Pushed_It: Gov. Tim Walz (D-Minn.), Democratic VP nominee
Notes: 2019 Trump OT rule expanded eligibility vs prior law; abandoned larger Obama expansion.

Claim: Violent crime was up under Donald Trump (as an overall Trump-term characterization).
Ended: Aug 7–8, 2024 (FactCheck.org: murders/aggravated assault up via 2020 spike; overall violent crime rate down 2016→2020)
Notes: FactCheck corrected its own initial rate direction Aug 8 using FBI 2022 CIUS.

Claim: The Trump administration resulted in a trade deficit that was 'one of the highest we've ever seen in the history of America.'
Ended: Sept 11, 2024 (FactCheck.org: Biden-era annual deficits exceeded Trump's peak)
Notes: BEA: 2020 Trump peak ~$654B; later Biden 12-month figures higher.

Claim: Biden-Harris digital ad featured Trump saying women must face 'some form of punishment' for abortion as if that remained his position (omitting same-day walk-back).
Ended: Sept 11, 2023 (FactCheck.org: ad misleadingly used retracted 2016 town-hall clip)
Notes: Trump same-day 2016 statement: physician responsible, woman a victim.

Claim: Trump is the only president other than Herbert Hoover who lost more jobs than he had when he began (ignoring COVID shock).
Ended: June 28, 2024 (FactCheck.org: net job loss driven by pandemic collapse; recovery underway before exit)
Notes: FactCheck section 'Biden Misleads on Jobs.'

Claim: Harris claimed Trump intends a 'sales tax' tariff plan that economists say would cost typical families about $4,000 a year (as the definitive estimate).
Ended: Sept 11, 2024 (FactCheck.org: $4,000 is high-end CAP estimate assuming 20% global + 60% China; other nonpartisan estimates much lower)
Notes: TPC/PIIE/Tax Foundation estimates ~$625–$1,700 range under common 10%/60% assumptions.

Claim: Donald Trump said he'd ban abortion across this country and will do it whether or not Congress is there (as current 2024 position).
Ended: Aug 7, 2024 (FactCheck.org: Trump said in 2024 he would leave abortion to states and would veto a national ban)
Deception_Form: outdated position presented as current pledge
Notes: Trump did support federal 20-week ban in 2016–18; 2024 video/interviews reject national ban.

Claim: Trump's plan would again give tax cuts only to billionaires and the biggest corporations (and blow up the deficit)—implying no benefit for other taxpayers.
Ended: Oct 18, 2024 (FactCheck.org: extending TCJA and other Trump proposals also benefit most/middle taxpayers)
Notes: Distinct from already-listed $5T billionaire-only framing; centers on Fox interview 'billionaires and biggest corporations' exclusivity.

Claim: Under Trump's administration, gender-affirming surgeries were available on a medical-necessity basis to people in the federal prison system (implying Trump-era practice matched Harris's position).
Ended: Oct 18, 2024 (FactCheck.org: BOP memo contemplated obligation, but first federal inmate surgeries occurred in 2022–23 under Biden)
Notes: Hormone therapy occurred; surgeries for federal inmates came later. Used to claim Trump policy 'no different.'
